Pop: The pop is unreal—better than any other Bataleon I've tried, including the already poppy Goliath and Beyond Medals. This helps average riders, like me, ollie easier than just about any other board out there 122. Catch-free ride: The 3bt makes the boards feel very catch-free and comfortable while retaining the power of full camber 123. Buttering: The flat section in the tip and tail locks in on a butter and makes it much easier than almost any other board I've tried with lifted sides in the nose/tail 124. Versatility — one-board quiver: The Goliath Plus is most suited to someone looking for a do-it-all, one-board-quiver type board. It has a consequence free feel, but can still carve, ride fast and has good spring out of turns and good pop 125. Freestyle capability: The Bataleon Goliath Plus is a pretty special board for jumping 126. Switch riding: Set up on reference stance, this rides switch incredibly well. It's not a true twin, but it's close 127. Powder float: Both the Goliath and Goliath Plus float very well for all-mountain boards. Despite the camber, TBT helps keep it afloat, especially when set back using full-sized discs 128. User review — light feel: Feels super light under foot. Super easy to turn and stable enough for my riding style 129. User review — Whitelines on the Plus: You can just feel how much lighter, faster and more reactive that core is. If you removed Triple Base from the equation, I actually think it'd be overkill for an all mountain snowboard. This kind of construction mixed with a full camber profile would be running into Jones Aviator 2.0 territory 130. Carving (moderate speeds): In terms of carving, it's particularly good for moderate speed and slower speed carves – not as good for higher speed carves 131. Uneven snow performance: While the pop is exceptional it comes at a pretty high price in soft uneven snow. This board bucks and bounces around in a pretty unsettling manner. It wants to launch into the air when you don't. While it's fine in smooth conditions, it can knock you off your line in bumpy conditions 132. Edge hold limitation: It's even worse than the Goliath in uneven snow and the edge hold is limited 133. Hard snow challenge: Bataleon boards are the most challenging boards with steel edges I've ridden in hard snow and they sap my confidence. In hard spring morning snow, I struggled to turn, even trying my best to twist and really put weight into the edges 134. The downside is it can feel a little loose in firm snow compared to traditional boards. Not as strong with edge hold in icy snow 135. Center-weighted requirement: You have to ride this perfectly center-weighted to engage the flat section, which is also the highest point off the snow. Once engaged, it flattens and allows you to get purchase on snow. It tracks well one-footing and flat basing—but can feel edgeless and washy if you don't stay centered 136. 3BT carve adjustment: Note that it's a different feeling on a carve – the engagement point of the edge is a little lower because of the 3BT. This isn't a problem, but just to know that if you were to go to a board without 3BT it would be a bit of an adjustment 137. The Bataleon Goliath Plus didn't feel Ultralight but is on the lighter side for sure. (We don't put in the exact weight because with wood cores, there is no consistency in a board's weight) 138. It was lighter on the scales vs the average and felt lighter than normal on snow than the Goliath, which is marginally heavier on the scales 139. Bataleon is pretty spot on with recommended weight but very liberal with recommended boot sizing 140. Key competitor: Jones Mountain Twin — The Mountain Twin is better than the Goliath in hard/icy conditions for sure. I wouldn't say the Goliath + was bad, but it's average 141. The Goliath Plus, for me, is better for buttering but only by a little bit vs the Mountain Twin, and I prefer Goliath Plus for jibbing 142.
